sentences.text: Juratyrant is a genus containing only one known species, Juratyrant langhami, which lived in England during the Late Jurassic period.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Dorset, England, in 1984 by the fossil collector Peter Langham.

Although mentioned in earlier papers, the species was not formally described until 2008 when Roger Benson assigned it to Stokesosaurus; Benson and Stephen Brusatte reclassified it into its own genus, Juratyrant, in 2013.
The genus is known from a single recorded fossil occurrence consisting of a partial skeleton with a complete pelvis, parts of the legs, and vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail.
Estimates of its size vary significantly; Zanno and Makovicky estimated in 2013 that Juratyrant weighed up to 648 kg, while Paul estimated in 2016 that it was 5 meters long and weighed 300 kg.
Juratyrant belongs to the class Reptilia and is classified within the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea and the family Stokesosauridae.
Juratyrant langhami lived between 149.3 and 149 million years ago in the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic in what is now Europe.

In 2013, Benson and Brusatte placed Juratyrant as a sister taxon to Stokesosaurus clevelandi within basal tyrannosauroids, but a 2013 study by Loewen et al. suggested it belonged to Proceratosauridae based on a shared narrow preacetabular notch. A 2016 analysis by Brusatte and Carr placed it as a tyrannosauroid slightly more advanced than Proceratosauridae and Dilong, whereas a 2025 study by Delcourt et al. found that equal-weight phylogenetic analyses placed Juratyrant as an ancestral megaraptoran, which would make it the oldest known record of that group.
